Rebuilding a dry stone wall

Posted on 3 March by Mara in Garden

The wall at the bottom of the field fell over in the January storms, about four metres of it, and I finally had a free weekend to put it back. A dry stone wall holds itself up by weight and friction alone, so the whole job is about choosing where each stone goes.

First the fallen stones were sorted into three heaps: big flat ones for the base, long ones for through stones that tie both faces together, and the small rubble that packs the middle. Sorting took most of Saturday morning, which surprised me.

The base course went into a shallow trench, each stone set with its longest side running into the wall rather than along it. Every course after that leans in slightly, a batter of about one in six, and every joint is crossed by the stone above it, one over two and two over one.

By Sunday evening the wall stood at its old height with the cope stones on top. It is not pretty yet, but it is solid: I stood on it, and it did not move. Next month I will tackle the gap by the gate.

Tags: walls, stone, weekend

3 comments

Tobias wrote: The one over two rule is the thing everyone forgets. Did you use a frame and string lines to keep the batter even?
Mara wrote: Yes, two wooden frames at each end with a line between them, moved up as each course went in.
Ilse wrote: Lovely work. Ours collapsed last year and we paid someone, I wish we had tried it ourselves.
